findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the duplicate-title metric reuses the pure `normalize_title` primitive (recent_creates.py:55) applied to durable CREATE events over the rolling-hour window, NOT the `duplicate_create_warning` function (which is bounded by its 600s journal and the suggest_duplicate_tickets config gate) — so 'cannot disagree' is achieved by sharing the normalizer, and the unit test drives `normalize_title` on both seams.
evidence: recent_creates.py:50 `RECENT_WINDOW_NS = 600 * 1_000_000_000` — duplicate_create_warning can only ever see a 600s window
recent_creates.py:148 `if not compose_config(cfg_root).verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets: return None` — the function is config-gated off by default
recent_creates.py:55 `def normalize_title(title: str)` — the pure, reusable normalized-title primitive with no window/config coupling
AC line 1 goal: 'do not invent a second definition that can disagree' — met by reusing normalize_title over durable CREATE events, not by calling duplicate_create_warning over a rolling hour
findings.finding: AC line 1 instructs reuse of the rule `duplicate_warning` uses ('reuse it'), but the function that computes it (`duplicate_create_warning`) is not a pure title predicate: it only sees a pruned 600s journal (RECENT_WINDOW_NS) and returns None when `verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets` is off. A host observer counting same-title creations over a ROLLING HOUR cannot reuse that function without inheriting a 600s horizon and a config gate, so the metric would disagree with the duplicate population by construction — the opposite of the AC's 'cannot disagree' goal. The reusable primitive that guarantees agreement is `normalize_title`.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, line 1 ('derived from the SAME rule duplicate_warning uses — reuse it'); Testing step 2; src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:55,134,148
scenarios: Implementer wires the hour-window duplicate metric onto duplicate_create_warning and it silently counts only same-title pairs within 600s, missing an 88/hr burst whose members are >600s apart
verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets is off in the observer's config context, so the reused function returns None and the metric reads zero during a real burst
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC line 1 and Testing step 2 to name `rebar._commands.recent_creates.normalize_title` as the shared rule, and state the observer counts same-normalized-title CREATE events from the store over the rolling hour (not via duplicate_create_warning, whose 600s journal and config gate make it unfit for an hour-window host metric).

findings.finding: The plan mandates the observer be independent of the bridge to avoid a dead-man inversion, but does not specify how the OBSERVER'S OWN liveness/failure is detected — recreating the same silent-failure risk one level up.
findings.location: 'The detector must be independent of the bridge' section
scenarios: The host-side observer crashes or its scheduled run stops; both duplicate and volume metrics go silent and no one is alerted to the blind spot
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC requiring an observer-heartbeat metric (or last-successful-publish timestamp) with its own missing-data alarm, so a dead observer pages rather than silently blinding the detectors.

Portability AC: 'local store read plus host metric publish; no dependence on any single CI provider.'
CI-as-venue rule: recurring work must state how it triggers without a specific CI system
findings.finding: The plan requires a host-side observer that publishes both metrics independently of the bridge and 'no dependence on any single CI provider', but never names the concrete recurring TRIGGER for that observer (operation-linked side-effect, cron on a workstation, or in-process fallback). The bridge itself runs in GitHub Actions; if the observer's only realistic trigger is also a CI schedule, a no-CI or non-GitHub-Actions venue would never run it and the metrics/alarms would never be evaluated.
findings.location: 'The detector must be independent of the bridge' section + Portability AC
scenarios: A rebar target with NO CI provider: the observer is never scheduled, so no duplicate/volume metric is ever published and the alarms never evaluate — the exact silence this ticket exists to remove persists.
A GitLab CI / Jenkins venue: a GitHub-Actions-only trigger never fires.
